t: You're on Juxon Street, in north Lambeth. It is named after William Juxon, a churchman who rose to the very top of the English church. He was Bishop of London from 1633 to 1646. He then became Archbishop of Canterbury in 1660 and held that office until he died in 1663. So his career spanned the turbulent years in between, and Lambeth, long associated with the archbishops, is a fitting place to find his name.
